sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h11 (notes/hooks.md). A list over witnesses whose membership is decided in body text, with look-alikes that take part in, pay for or speak for members who run the scheme. Same shape as the family's measured Medium (aq-03950 q02, Low 0/5 · Medium 2/6), except that here each member rests on the witness's own words. Target medium; hard is also open (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Quick test 2026-10-13: survived (user report, no panel). No difficulty run yet.
- Dependency plan: D02 Q138 and Q157 put the reporters on Reach's staff (Higgerson). D03 Q257 puts them on the Liverpool Echo's (Breslin) and D03 Q255 on Social Spider's (Floyd). Three names.
- Universe: the twenty witnesses in the report's list. Every sentence naming the scheme ("LDR", "local democracy", "democracy report") in the three transcripts was read by speaker (script, 2026-10-13). In: Higgerson, Breslin, Floyd. Out, with the deciding words: Hutchinson, D02 Q138 "They are managed by National World"; Davies, D02 Q196 "employed by local commercial operators"; Abbott, D03 Q271 "our members employ"; Hancock, D03 Q256 "Nub News gets access to that"; Perkins, D03 Q271 "We can't access it because our journalists are volunteers"; Meredith, D01 Q23 "Those are employed by my members"; Powell, D01 Q32 "We have only one station that has a contract"; Cantwell-Corn, D01 Q108 "We were not eligible at that time for having a LDR reporter within our newsroom"; Steers, D01 Q65 would like stations "bidding to hold some of those contracts". Fenton, Heawood, Stanistreet, Brock, Morrison-Bell and Severinson speak about the scheme or not at all, never as an employer of its reporters. The Minister and her official (fourth hearing, no transcript) speak for a government department.
- Necessity: without D02 nothing shows Reach's reporters through a witness (answer: Breslin, Floyd). Without D03 neither the Echo's nor Social Spider's are shown (answer: Higgerson). D01 holds only witnesses who are left out, so it is not ticked and no step leans on it; removing it leaves the answer unchanged. D04 says Reach took 75 reporters and names Notts TV, which sent no witness; it never mentions the Echo's or Social Spider's reporters.
- Selected-lever checks: which-items decoy named and failed (Hutchinson: part of the scheme, "our" reporters, another publisher's staff). Wrong lists recomputed: scheme users added, Breslin, Floyd, Higgerson, Hutchinson, Hancock, Cantwell-Corn (six); membership bodies added, Breslin, Floyd, Higgerson, Abbott, Powell, Meredith (six); funder added, four with Davies; the publisher the report names alone, Higgerson; own-word "employ" required, Higgerson only or with Abbott.
- Targeted failure modes: Wrong kind of entity / Wrong members in a list: a scheme partner (Hutchinson), the funder (Davies) and a membership body (Abbott) taken for an employer of the reporters; wrong lists of four to six names. Unobserved so far: the quick test gave no panel. To be matched to the wrong answers actually observed after the first run, before Submit.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (no arithmetic, no dates).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: searching "local democracy" gives over seventy sentences across the three transcripts; no passage lists who employs the reporters. The report's allocation sentence (Reach, Newsquest, JPI Media) names publishers, not witnesses. The bundle overview mentions the scheme and "165 local democracy reporters" but no employer. Shortest route: the four passages in Steps 1-3.
- Precision/readings: (1) taking part in the scheme or using its copy read as having reporters: adds Hutchinson, Hancock, Cantwell-Corn. "on its own staff" rejects it; still likely on a quick read, and the form's "One defensible answer" check and the run will show whether solvers take it. (2) A membership body counted for its members: adds Abbott, Powell, Meredith. "its own staff" rejects it. Powell is the weakest exclusion: a reader who takes the Local TV Network to be its stations could add him; the report says the scheme was valuable "among its members" and Powell speaks of "our members". (3) The funder counted: Davies says "employed by local commercial operators". (4) Breslin left out because she never says "employ": she says "our LDRs, our political editor manages them". (5) Floyd left out: his clause sits in an answer about grant funds. (6) "worked for" read as employment only: all three hold posts at their organisations (editor, director, chief audience officer).
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (notes/intake.json). All four documents read in full. The absent fourth hearing has two government witnesses; neither can change the list.
- Style/set review: 28 words, one ask, a three-name list in surname order. Shares Doc 3's scheme passages with sketch i03 (a salary floor): at most one of the two is submitted. No answer path in common with q01 (grant fund) or i02 (who the BBC's witness answered).
- Warnings answered: origin is claude (accurate; the export tool takes user only, and the question reaches the form in the user's words). single-passage: the passage the floor matched is the report's witness list (D04), which prints all twenty witnesses' names and titles on adjacent lines; it says nothing about the scheme, so it does not hold the answer. Format: the quick-tested sketch ended "List them in any order."; the floor reports that this tail drew the form's rule-10 advisory on aq-03736 q02, so rev 0 asks for surname order, which the gold already had. No other word of the question changed. The reasoning quotes Floyd in two parts so that the document's dash is not carried into the form.
sections.question: Judging by all the evidence the committee heard, which witnesses, if any, worked for an organisation with local democracy reporters on its own staff? List them alphabetically by surname.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, David Higgerson, Chief Audience Officer of Reach): asked about the scheme, he says "As a company, Reach spends more on delivering the LDRS scheme than it receives from the BBC to fund it." Asked about turnover among these reporters, he says "we have the Teesside contract there and we also have Northumberland and Tyneside". Reach holds the contracts and the reporters are on its staff, so Higgerson belongs in the list (third component).
Step 2. Source input (Doc 4, Maria Breslin, Editor of the Liverpool Echo): she says "so we support our LDRs, our political editor manages them". The Echo has the reporters on its own staff, so Breslin belongs in the list (first component).
Step 3. Source input (Doc 4, David Floyd, Director of Social Spider CIC): he says the "Local Democracy Reporter scheme funds posts" and adds "we have two of them and it is great". Social Spider has such posts itself, so Floyd belongs in the list (second component).
Step 4. Decoy (Doc 3, Paul Hutchinson, co-founder of the Bedford Independent): he says "We are part of the LDRS and make sure that local council meetings are covered." He also says "We have a fantastic relationship with our LDRS reporters in our patch. They are managed by National World." The reporters are another publisher's staff, so Hutchinson is left out.
Step 5. Not counted (Doc 3, Rhodri Talfan Davies of the BBC): the BBC pays for the scheme, but he says its journalists are "funded from the licence fee but employed by local commercial operators". The funder has none on its own staff, so Davies is left out.
Step 6. Not counted (Doc 4, Matt Abbott of the Independent Community News Network): he says "I think our members employ perhaps a dozen Local Democracy Reporters themselves". The reporters are on the members' staff, not the network's, so Abbott is left out. The other witnesses in Doc 3 and Doc 4 either do not speak about the scheme or say that they only use its copy.
Step 7. Final answer (Doc 3 and Doc 4): Maria Breslin, David Floyd, David Higgerson.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong kind of entity
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Wrong kind of entity: Doc 3's Paul Hutchinson says "We are part of the LDRS", yet his reporters are "managed by National World"; the BBC only funds, and Doc 4's network speaks for members. Adding them gives four to six names. The gold keeps the three employers' witnesses.
